extracted.intended_audience: Applicants, institutional administrators, mentors, and peer reviewers involved in NIH Career Development (K) awards and related NIH grants operations
extracted.subtask_description: NIH Grants Policy guidance covering Responsible Conduct of Research (RCR) instruction requirements, review criteria, allowable costs, budget formats (including modular budgets), administrative requirements, and other terms and conditions for Career Development (CDA/K) awards and related modular applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCR instruction modality
rubrics_metrics.description: Video conferencing may be incorporated into RCR instruction but should be utilized in a way that fosters discussion, active learning, engagement, and interaction; video conferencing should not be the sole means for meeting RCR instruction requirement except in special short-term training programs or unusual and well-justified circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions may consider video conferencing options; a plan employing only video conferencing will not be considered acceptable except for short-term programs or exceptional justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCR subject matter: conflict of interest and commitment
rubrics_metrics.description: Instruction should include conflict of interest – personal, professional, and financial – and conflict of commitment in allocating time, effort, or other research resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This topic is one of several that have been incorporated into most acceptable RCR plans; coverage should be substantive rather than perfunctory.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCR subject matter: human subjects, vertebrate animals, and lab safety
rubrics_metrics.description: Instruction should include policies regarding human subjects, live vertebrate animal subjects in research, and safe laboratory practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courses that only cover clinical research or animal care are generally not sufficient to cover all aspects of RCR instruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCR subject matter: mentor/mentee responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Instruction should cover mentor/mentee responsibilities and relationships.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mentoring responsibilities are a core RCR topic and should be addressed in formal and informal instruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCR subject matter: safe research environments
rubrics_metrics.description: Instruction should address safe research environments (e.g., free of sexual, racial, ethnic, disability, and other discriminatory harassment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Safe environment topics may include institutional policies and practical measures to ensure respectful, nondiscriminatory workplaces.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCR subject matter: collaborative research
rubrics_metrics.description: Instruction should include collaborative research including collaborations with industry and investigators and institutions in other countries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Topics should cover responsibilities, agreements, and challenges of multi-institution and international collaborations.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCR subject matter: peer review responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Instruction should cover peer review, including the responsibility for maintaining confidentiality and security in peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize ethical conduct, confidentiality obligations, and conflicts in the peer review process.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCR subject matter: data acquisition, analysis, and recordkeeping
rubrics_metrics.description: Instruction should include data acquisition and analysis; laboratory tools (e.g., tools for analyzing data and creating or working with digital images); recordkeeping practices, including methods such as electronic laboratory notebooks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address best practices, reproducibility, and proper documentation methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCR subject matter: secure and ethical data use and sharing
rubrics_metrics.description: Instruction should address secure and ethical data use; data confidentiality, management, sharing and ownership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include policies and practical guidance on data stewardship, privacy, and data sharing obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCR subject matter: research misconduct policies
rubrics_metrics.description: Instruction should include research misconduct and policies for handling misconduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cover definitions, reporting procedures, investigations, and institutional responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCR subject matter: responsible authorship and publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Instruction should include responsible authorship and publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Topics should include authorship criteria, plagiarism, corrections/retractions, and publication ethics.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCR subject matter: scientist as responsible member of society
rubrics_metrics.description: Instruction should include the scientist as a responsible member of society, contemporary ethical issues in biomedical research, and the environmental and societal impacts of scientific research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address broader ethical and societal implications of research and scientist responsibilities beyond the laboratory.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCR curricular sufficiency caveat
rubrics_metrics.description: Courses related to professional ethics, ethical issues in clinical research, or research involving vertebrate animals may form part of RCR instruction but generally are not sufficient to cover all aspects of responsible research conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions should ensure RCR programs comprehensively cover the enumerated topics rather than relying solely on related specialty courses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Faculty participation in RCR instruction
rubrics_metrics.description: Mentors and other appropriate faculty are highly encouraged to contribute to both formal and informal instruction in RCR; rotation of training faculty as course directors, instructors, and/or discussion leaders may help achieve broad faculty participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Informal instruction occurs in laboratory interactions year-round; institutional Career Awards may use faculty as discussion leaders, speakers, lecturers, and course directors.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCR duration requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Instruction should involve substantive contact hours; acceptable programs generally involve at least eight contact hours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Semester-long series of seminars/programs may be more effective than single seminars or one-day workshops for depth and consolidation of learning.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCR frequency requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: RCR instruction should be undertaken at least once during each career stage and at a frequency of no less than once every four years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions are encouraged to provide ongoing and discipline-specific training as individuals progress; advanced trainees may receive more tailored training relevant to their field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget: CDA allowable cost types
rubrics_metrics.description: CDAs provide limited costs, generally covering applicable salary and fringe benefits for the candidate and a fixed amount for research development support; costs must be consistent with Federal cost principles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Salary amounts and research development costs vary by CDA program and IC; consult the relevant NOFO for allowable costs and limitations; include budget justification per Application Guide and NOFO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget submission: senior/key person and research development support
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed budget information is required as part of the initial application but limited to senior/key person information for the candidate and the total amount of requested research development support in budget section F.1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A budget justification is required to describe research development support costs; follow Application Guide and NOFO instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indirect costs for CDAs
rubrics_metrics.description: Indirect costs for CDAs are provided at a rate of 8% of modified total direct costs, except for certain cases (e.g., R00 phase and certain State/local/tribal entities).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State and local agencies and federally recognized Indian tribes may be eligible for full indirect cost reimbursement; see NOFO and cost principles for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scored review criterion: Candidate
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers evaluate the candidate in terms of likelihood to develop/maintain a strong research program; a separate score is given for this criterion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider the candidate's qualifications, research record, potential for independence, and career stage; specifics may vary by CDA program and are detailed in the NOFO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scored review criterion: Career Development Plan/Career Goals & Objectives/Plan to Provide Mentoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers assess the quality of the career development plan, goals and objectives, and the plan to provide mentoring; a separate score is given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate clarity, feasibility, training plan, timeline, and mentoring structure; refer to NOFO for program-specific expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scored review criterion: Research Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers evaluate the research plan's scientific and technical merit; a separate score is given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess significance, approach, feasibility, innovation, and how the research supports career development objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scored review criterion: Mentor(s), Co-Mentor(s), Consultant(s), Collaborator(s) and Mentoring Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers assess the qualifications and commitment of the mentor(s), co-mentors, consultants, and collaborators and the mentoring plan; a separate score is given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider mentor track record, mentoring environment, and appropriateness of mentorship for career development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scored review criterion: Environment and Institutional Commitment to the Candidate
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers evaluate the institutional environment and commitment to the candidate; a separate score is given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess institutional support, protected time, resources, and how the environment fosters the candidate's development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional review criterion: Protection of Human Subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: As applicable, reviewers will evaluate protection of human subjects while determining scientific and technical merit, but will not give a separate score for this item.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the NOFO for details on human subjects protections and how they affect review and funding decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional review criterion: Inclusion of Women, Minorities, and Individuals Across the Lifespan
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will consider plans for inclusion across sex/gender, race/ethnicity, and ages as applicable; not scored separately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to NOFO and NIH inclusion policies for expectations and required justifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional review criterion: Vertebrate Animals
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of vertebrate animals will be evaluated as applicable; not scored separately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide required animal welfare and justification information per policy and NOFO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional review criterion: Biohazards
rubrics_metrics.description: Biohazard issues will be evaluated as applicable; not scored separately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address biosafety and institutional oversight where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional review items: Resubmission, Renewal, Revision Applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Resubmission, renewal, and revision applications will be evaluated as applicable but are not given separate scores.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See NOFO for specific expectations for these application types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional review consideration: Training in the Responsible Conduct of Research
rubrics_metrics.description: Training in RCR will be addressed by reviewers as an additional consideration but will not receive a separate score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure RCR plans meet NIH expectations described elsewhere in policy (topics, duration, frequency, faculty participation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional review consideration: Select Agents
rubrics_metrics.description: Select agent use will be evaluated as applicable but not scored separately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide required approvals and biosafety documentation where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional review consideration: Authentication of Key Biological/Chemical Resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Authentication of key resources (e.g., cell lines, biological/chemical reagents) will be addressed as an additional consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include plans for authentication to ensure reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional review consideration: Resource Sharing Plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Plans for resource sharing will be considered but not scored separately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include data sharing, model organism sharing, and other resource-sharing plans as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional review consideration: Budget and Period of Support
rubrics_metrics.description: Budget and period of support will be addressed by reviewers as additional considerations (not scored).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers will not give separate scores but will note if budgetary requests are appropriate for the proposed work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of action procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Candidates receive e-mail notifications when the SRG recommendation/impact score and the summary statement are available in the eRA Commons; PO may notify applicant about final review recommendation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Direct questions about initial review recommendations and funding possibilities to the designated IC PO, not the SRO of the SRG.

rubrics_metrics.name: Period of support length and continuation criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Awards are for a period of 3 to 5 years and provide support for salary and research-development support costs; support beyond the first year is based on NIH assessment of effectiveness and recipient’s annual progress report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continuation is contingent upon future Federal appropriations; mentored CDAs are not renewable (non-mentored CDAs may be renewable at IC discretion); K99/R00 and some K22 programs have distinct phases with phase II contingent on specific criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Salary and fringe benefit requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Requested salary and fringe benefits must follow institutional policies applied consistently to individuals in like circumstances and be supported by acceptable accounting principles; CDA salary amounts must be based on the investigator’s institutional base salary prorated for their commitment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Salary requests must relate to existing salary structures; confirmation of costs may be required prior to award; salary caps apply and vary by IC/NOFO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Salary supplementation rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipient institution may supplement the NIH salary contribution on the CDA up to a level consistent with the institution's salary scale; supplementation must be from non-Federal sources and must not require extra duties that interfere with CDA goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PHS funds may not be used for supplementation; supplementation for effort not directly committed to the CDA is allowable under certain conditions if specific aims differ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unallowable salary supports
rubrics_metrics.description: Salary support for ancillary personnel (e.g., administrative assistance or secretarial support) on CDAs is not allowable; salary support for mentors is not allowable on individual mentored CDAs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Salary support for research technicians or study coordinators for clinical studies is generally allowable but budgeted as part of Research Development Support Costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Development Support Costs definition
rubrics_metrics.description: CDAs may include a fixed amount for research development support costs commonly used for supplies, equipment, technical personnel, travel to meetings/training, tuition/fees, and computational services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amount varies by IC and program; detail these costs in the budget justification as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal preparation costs allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: Mentored CDA programs may allow effort and costs devoted to proposal preparation for subsequent research support to be charged to a mentored CDA award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such costs can be considered part of the awarded effort commitment or an increase to that commitment with allowable salary as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indirect cost policy detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Career awards (other than certain phases and entities) receive indirect costs at 8% of modified total direct costs; State/local agencies and federally recognized Indian tribes may receive full indirect reimbursement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State universities/hospitals are not considered governmental agencies for this policy; check specifics in NOFO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rebudgeting authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Funds awarded on CDAs may typically be rebudgeted within direct cost categories without prior approval; restrictions may be noted in the NoA; rebudgeting of salary funds freed from other NIH grants may require prior approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions must ensure rebudgeting remains within approved scope and institutional salary scale and under legislative salary caps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Carryover authority for CDA funds
rubrics_metrics.description: Individual CDAs generally have automatic carryover authority unless otherwise noted; most Institutional CDAs require prior approval to carry over funds; the NoA will specify requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For K99/R00, carryover from K99 to R00 may be allowed if K99 was extramurally funded; consult awarding IC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting requirement consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to comply with reporting requirements and timely submission of required forms may result in expenditure disallowance or delay in continuation funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adhere to RPPR, FFR, and closeout timelines to avoid financial/admin penalties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Progress report format and submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Most individual CDA awards under SNAP must submit progress reports using the RPPR module in eRA Commons; for RPPR submissions, the IDP requirement for Non-Competing Continuation Progress Reports applies; non-SNAP awards use PHS 2590 instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final RPPR must be submitted within 120 days after end of grant support as part of closeout.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal Financial Report (FFR) requirement for SNAP CDAs
rubrics_metrics.description: For individual CDAs awarded under SNAP, an annual electronic FFR is not required; only a final FFR is required at the end of the project period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow administrative requirements sections in IIA for financial reporting specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Closeout requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Closeout requirements in IIA apply to all Individual CDAs; Institutional Scientist Development Programs are excepted from final invention statement (K12s & KL2s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit required final reports and documents per IIA timelines and instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post closeout evaluation data requests
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH may request information after completion of awards to assess program effectiveness, including employment history, publications, support, honors, and professional activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients should expect periodic updates and maintain records to support such requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change of recipient/transfer rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Approval of the NIH awarding IC is required for transfer of the CDA to another institution or for project changes; individual mentored and non-mentored CDAs may not be transferred to another PD/PI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mentored CDAs transferring institutions must have a mentor at the new institution and provide supporting documentation; consult NIH program and grants management staff when considering transfers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to extend final budget period without additional funds
rubrics_metrics.description: CDA recipients may extend the final budget period of a project period without additional funds for up to 12 months; all terms and programmatic requirements apply during the extension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full-time appointment and minimum effort requirements must continue for the extension period; consider these requirements when requesting additional time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporary off-site career development experience rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Temporary career development experiences at other institutions including foreign labs may be permitted if directly related to the award; local institutional approval suffices for <=3 months, prior written IC approval required for >3 months up to 12 months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special information required for certain awards (e.g., K99/R00, K22, K05, K07, K24, K12, KL2) to address impact on award goals and mentoring; support continues during off-site experience if approved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leave policies for CDA recipients
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutional leave policies apply for vacation, sick, parental leave, etc.; a leave/sabbatical greater than three months must be requested and approved in writing by the NIH awarding IC; leave less than 3 months requires institutional prior approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For certain awards (K99, K05, K07, K24, K12, KL2), additional assurances or descriptions of impact on award goals are required for leaves >3 months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unpaid leave limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Leave without award support may not exceed 12 months, requires prior written approval of the awarding component, and will be granted only with justification; award will be placed in a no-cost extension and no charges to the grant allowed during unpaid leave.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continued health insurance coverage may be allowable if per institutional policy; unpaid leave does not reduce total months of program support eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of Appointment for Institutional CDAs (PHS 2271)
rubrics_metrics.description: For initial appointment of K12 or KL2 scholars, Program Director may submit a Statement of Appointment (Form PHS 2271) to document scholar appointments when required by the NOFO; when required, submission must use xTrain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy varies by IC and is specified in the NOFO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Early termination authority and process
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH may terminate a CDA early if the recipient materially fails to comply with award terms or to carry out the purpose; NIH will notify recipient in writing of determination, reasons, effective date, and right to appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult NIH program and grants management staff when termination is being considered; institutions should notify awarding IC as early as possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other income: retention and disposition of professional fees
rubrics_metrics.description: CDA recipients may retain royalties and fees from incidental activities (scholarly writing, advisory service, honoraria, clinical practice fees) provided activities remain incidental and consistent with institutional policies; other income must be assigned to the recipient institution for disposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institution may expend funds for salary supplementation or research, or remit to U.S. Treasury; adequate records on source, receipt, and disposition must be maintained per 2 CFR Part 200.307.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modular application applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: Modular procedures are required for certain grant mechanisms that request up to $250,000 direct costs per year (excluding consortium indirect costs), including R01/U01, R03, R21/UH2, R34/U34, and R15/UA5; modular procedures do not apply to SBIR/STTR Phase I (R43/R41) or foreign organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific grant mechanisms or IC guidelines may indicate different module allowances; check applicable NOFOs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modular budget structure and submission requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Modular applications request direct costs in $25,000 modules up to $250,000 per year; applicants must use the PHS 398 Modular Budget Component in the electronic SF424 (R&R) submission and should not provide the standard SF424 Research and Related Budget Component.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No individual salary information should be provided; use current legislatively imposed salary limitation when determining the number of modules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modular budget: consortium and contractual cost justification
rubrics_metrics.description: When applicable, a separate budget justification must address consortium/contractual costs (including applicable indirect costs) rounded to the nearest $1,000 and list individuals/organizations, level of effort (person months), roles, and indicate whether collaborating organization is foreign or domestic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide narrative describing consortium arrangements; follow modular component guidance in Application Guide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justification for year-to-year modular variance
rubrics_metrics.description: If requesting different numbers of modules in different years, applicants must provide additional narrative budget justification explaining substantial changes in expected activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include major equipment purchases in year one that justify higher budget for that year; NIH may request detailed budgets during Just-in-Time review.

rubrics_metrics.name: SRG budget evaluation for modular applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Scientific Review Groups evaluate modular budgets on the basis of a general expert estimate of total effort and resources required; recommended adjustments are expressed in entire modules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If SRG recommends budget adjustment, it will be in whole-module terms; for applications under consideration, ICs may request other support and additional budget info before award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award budget characteristics for modular awards
rubrics_metrics.description: The award budget will be a noncategorical budget specifying approved total direct costs and indirect costs, if applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients have discretion in how to allocate and account for costs within institutional systems but must follow applicable cost principles and NIHGPS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-award administration for modular awards
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutions may allocate and account for modular award costs as they see fit within organizational accounting systems, subject to cost principles; significant rebudgeting provision (change of scope indicator) does not apply to modular grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative supplements must provide detailed (non-modular) budgets; Competing Revisions should use the modular budget component.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conference grants support criteria (R13/U13)
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH supports scientific meetings, conferences, and workshops relevant to its scientific mission and public health under R13 and U13 activity codes; support is contingent on IC interests and priorities and applications must follow published receipt dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generally NIH will not award conference grants unless Federal award date can precede conference start date; awarding after the conference requires documentation that funding of post-conference activities is consistent with approved application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conference definitions (conference/scientific meeting/domestic/international)
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH adopts definitions: a conference disseminates technical information beyond recipient; scientific meeting gathers to coordinate/exchange info; international conference is open to participants in two or more countries other than U.S./Canada; domestic conference is held in U.S./Canada primarily for U.S./U.S.-Canadian participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definitions affect eligibility and applicable policies; consult chapter for applicability and eligibility criteria.
